title: Normalize tool parameters and backcompat translation layer
creator: Devon Patel
description: Implement a lightweight runtime compatibility shim that deterministically translates OpenAI-style tool calls into Redwood legacy function invocations. Focus areas: parameter name normalization (case/alias mapping), argument coercion (types and shapes), positional vs named argument mapping, and stable naming rules for metrics/tracing. This is to avoid requiring callers to change existing code when we add new structured output/streaming tool semantics.
background: We continue to support a mix of integrators: some send 'tools' (OpenAI-style) defined with a name and json_schema, others call Redwood's older 'functions' surface which expects a different name format and typed params. Past attempts created multiple small adapters; they cause divergence in runtime routing and metrics tagging. A single normalization layer will centralize logic and reduce bugs in fallback behavior (e.g., when model picks an alias name or uses camelCase payloads).
acceptance_criteria: Requests with OpenAI-style tool payloads are translated to legacy function contract with >99.9% fidelity for our canonical test harness
Alias mapping supports at least three configurable patterns: exact match, case-insensitive, and explicit alias registry
Type coercion supports string->number, number->string, and shallow array/object normalization where schema permits
No dropped KV-cache or streaming metadata during translation; streaming tokens preserve associated tool metadata
Automated regression suite added to runtime-compat CI that asserts semantics for 50+ sample tool schemas and 120 sample calls
design_notes: Place shim in routing layer before model selection so fallbacks can target compatible model variants
Use a deterministic canonicalization function: lower_snake_case(name) + stable suffix for legacy function if needed
Maintain a runtime alias registry backed by a small protobuf-based snapshot loaded from Config Store; updates do not require router restart
Implement lightweight schema-aware coercer: validate input against target param schema, attempt safe coercions, and record coercion events to metrics
Expose translation details in response debug header X-RW-Tool-Translation for customers when debug mode enabled
Avoid heavy JSON Schema evaluation at runtime; use precompiled reduced schemas for common types to keep latency impact <2ms median
implementation_plan: Spike (2d): build prototype that maps a sample of 20 OpenAI tool definitions to legacy function calls and measures latency overhead
Phase 1 (4d): core canonicalizer + alias registry + simple coercion rules; integrate into router as opt-in feature gate
Phase 2 (6d): add schema precompiler, streaming metadata propagation, and debug header support
Phase 3 (4d): roll out alias registry UI hooks for Console and add migration tool to generate suggested aliases from customer usage
Safety: add opt-out header for customers that want original payloads preserved
Performance: add microbenchmark harness and include in runtime perf dashboard
rollout_plan: Canary: enable shim for internal seed orgs and Redwood dev tenant for 48 hours
Gradual ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% of hostnames over 7 days with rollback window at each step
Fallback: if coercion error rate >0.5% or latency P95 increase >5ms, rollback to previous routing behavior
Post-rollout: run 24h regression job comparing outputs across old pipeline vs shimmed pipeline for critical prompt suites
test_plan: Unit tests for canonicalizer edge cases (unicode, punctuation, long names)
Property tests for idempotence of translation (translating twice yields same canonical result)
Integration tests: sample apps calling tools and functions endpoints asserting identical function invocation logs
Load test: 10k RPS with mixed short/long sequences to confirm added latency <2ms median and memory <2% increase
Security test: ensure no extra PII is introduced into logs/headers by translation process
monitoring_and_metrics: Dashboard: per-tenant translation heatmap and coercion-event timeline
